title: SF Home Where Landlord Allegedly Shot Tenant Now Available to Rent
text:
A San Francisco home that was the site of a gruesome killing between a landlord and his tenant is now available to be rented again. The home's listed price is $6,300 a month, and it has a range of features including hardwood floors, natural lighting, a large private backyard, and a private garage. However, the home's dark history has left many wondering how it's possible for the property to be rented again so soon. The landlord, Phillipe Chagniot, allegedly shot and killed his tenant, Eric Bigone, on May 17. Bigone's son, Dino Bigone, filed a wrongful death lawsuit against Chagniot, alleging that the landlord took his life because he wanted to sell the home and avoid reporting the earnings on his taxes. Chagniot had been demanding that Bigone pay his rent in cash and had been sending him unlawful notices to enter the property without notice, as part of a campaign of harassment aimed at causing Bigone to vacate the premises. Despite this, the home is now back on the market and available for rent.
A three-bedroom, two-bathroom home in San Francisco's Outer Sunset neighborhood has gone back on the rental market despite being the site of a gruesome killing.
The home's landlord, Phillipe Chagniot, a retired dentist, allegedly shot and killed his tenant, Eric Bigone, on May 17. According to a wrongful death lawsuit filed by Bigone's son, Dino Bigone, the landlord took his life because he wanted to sell the home and avoid reporting the earnings on his taxes.
Chagniot had been demanding that Bigone pay his rent in cash and had been sending him unlawful notices to enter the property without notice, as part of a campaign of harassment aimed at causing Bigone to vacate the premises. The rental is advertised as 'a beautifully updated single-family home in San Francisco's desirable Outer Sunset neighborhood' on Zillow, and includes features like hardwood floors, natural lighting, a large private backyard, and a private garage.
However, the home's dark history has left many wondering how it's possible for the property to be rented again so soon. Chagniot was arrested on May 27 and charged with murder and other counts, and remains in custody without bail, according to jail records. Attorney Michael Cardoza, who previously represented Chagniot, confirmed that the alleged killer is no longer his client, but did not disclose why they parted ways.
As for Bigone, his death came after a long battle with harassment from his landlord. The tenant had been renting the home for $3,200 a month, but Chagniot had demanded that he pay in cash to avoid reporting the earnings on his taxes. Bigone's son, Dino, said that his father tried to avoid paying Chagniot the cash but the landlord continued to send him unlawful notices to enter the property without notice.
Bigone ended up obtaining an attorney to help navigate the situation, and the attorney managed to get Chagniot to provide an address for the tenant to send his rent checks to. But even after Bigone obtained the necessary documents, Chagniot continued to harass him. The landlord allegedly spray-painted several cameras in the area to try and conceal his actions, before ultimately shooting Bigone in the back of the head with a silenced MAC-20 submachine gun.
Bigone's security deposit was never returned, and his family was left to deal with the aftermath of his death. Despite this, the home is now back on the market and available for rent, with a listed price of $6,300 a month. The future of the property is unclear, but one thing is certain: the case of Phillipe Chagniot and Eric Bigone will not soon be forgotten. The listing for the home emphasizes its desirable location, beautiful updates, and numerous features.
However, it leaves out any mention of the home's dark history. Surveillance footage captured Chagniot with a silenced MAC-20 submachine gun in hand at the time of the killing, police said. Chagniot then 'stood over Bigone and shot him again' before he 'casually rode off on his bicycle' to a home he shared with his wife Barbara, the lawsuit read.
Chagniot has not revealed a motive for the alleged deadly attack, but according to the lawsuit, Bigone's son said that the landlord took his life because he wanted to sell the home. Bigone rented out the home in 2023 for $3,200 a month, and when he did, Chagniot 'demanded' that the payment be made in cash so he could avoid reporting the earnings on his taxes, the lawsuit claimed
